output:
Short answer: choose an LED task lamp with good efficacy (high lumens per watt), dimming/controls, and an ENERGY STAR or equivalent efficiency rating. From our catalog memory the Harbor Task Lamp is a candidate, but I don’t have verified technical specs stored — you should confirm wattage, lumens and certifications before purchasing.

Why an LED task lamp
- LEDs give the most energy savings for desk lighting vs incandescent/halogen (typical LEDs use a small fraction of the power for the same light output). Evidence available: general industry data about LED efficiency (not specific to the Harbor product). Claim to verify: exact percent energy savings depends on the lamp model and the baseline lamp type — check manufacturer datasheets or ENERGY STAR listings for precise numbers.

Which features matter (and why)
- Lamp luminous flux (lumens): determines useful light output. For desk tasks aim for ~400–800 lumens at the desk surface (verify with manufacturer photometrics).
- Efficacy (lumens per watt): higher lm/W = more light per electricity used. Prefer ≥80 lm/W for good efficiency; many modern LEDs are 80–120+ lm/W. Evidence: efficacy is the metric manufacturers publish; you must verify numbers on spec sheets.
- Dimming and multiple brightness levels: saves energy when full output isn’t needed and extends lamp lifetime. Verify whether the lamp’s dimming method is flicker-free and whether dimming reduces power draw linearly (some drivers don’t).
- Color temperature and CRI: 3000–4000 K is comfortable for offices; CRI ≥80 is usually adequate for accurate color. These affect comfort/productivity but not energy use much.
- Controls/automation (motion sensor, scheduling, smart controls): can reduce wasted-on lighting. Verify presence and power use of always-on sensors (some sensors draw small standby power).
- Certification: ENERGY STAR (or equivalent) confirms tested efficiency and performance. Verify the product is listed in the certification database.
- Build/adjustability: good arm articulation, stable base, and glare control improve task lighting so lower output can still be effective.

Catalog product note: Harbor Task Lamp
- Memory found an item named “Harbor Task Lamp.” Evidence available: only the product name in our catalog memory. No provenance or specification data is available in the memory extract I consulted.
- Claims to verify before buying: whether it is LED, the wattage, lumens, lm/W efficacy, dimming, color temperature/CRI, ENERGY STAR (or equivalent) certification, warranty and return policy, and any smart features. If you want, I can look up those specs for you.

Quick selection checklist you can use when comparing models
1. Is it LED? (Yes → proceed)
2. Wattage and lumens shown → calculate lm/W. Prefer ≥80 lm/W.
3. Is it dimmable? Do reviews mention flicker?
4. Color temp and CRI (3000–4000 K and CRI ≥80 recommended).
5. Certifications (ENERGY STAR or similar).
6. Controls (sensor, timer, app) and any standby power use.
7. Warranty, return policy, and customer reviews for build quality.

If you want, I can:
- Pull full specs and provenance for the Harbor Task Lamp from our catalog (or elsewhere) and compare it to 2–3 other specific models.
- Recommend specific models for budget, style, or smart-control preferences.

Which would you like me to do next? (If you want product comparisons, tell me budget, style, and any must-have features.)
